Prune your vine in midwinter when dormant to prevent it from bleeding sap and losing its strength.
Pinch out the growing tips in midsummer to focus all of your vine's energy into ripening the grapes.
Keep a sharp eye out for powdery mildew during wet UK summers and space branches out for airflow.
Mulch with well-rotted manure in spring to feed the soil but keep it clear of the main woody stem.

items.name: Grape 'Ortega'

Cut away leaves around the grape bunches in August to let the British autumn sun ripen the berries.
Water deeply at the base only during dry spells, keeping the foliage dry to stop powdery mildew.

Mulch with well-rotted manure in early spring to feed the soil and lock in moisture.

items.name: Grape 'Seyval Blanc'

Prune hard in midwinter to prevent bleeding and keep this vigorous vine to its allotted space.
Plant your Seyval Blanc in your sunniest south-facing spot to help the grapes ripen in UK summers.
Thin out the dense summer foliage in August so the precious UK sunshine can actually reach the fruit.
Keep a sharp eye out for powdery mildew in damp weather and space your branches widely for airflow.
Feed with high-potash tomato food weekly once flowers appear to boost your final autumn harvest.
items.description: Hybrid white wine grape, hardy.

items.name: Grape 'Sieger'
items.growersTips:
Plant this early-ripening grape in your sunniest, south-facing UK wall to guarantee sweet berries.
Prune in midwinter when fully dormant to prevent the vine from bleeding sap and losing its strength.
Pinch out the growing tips of fruiting shoots two leaves beyond the grape bunches in midsummer.
Protect the ripening pink berries with fine netting in late August before hungry UK wasps find them.
Grow this vine in well-drained, chalky or gravelly soil, avoiding rich compost to prevent leafiness.
items.description: German outdoor white wine grape.

items.name: Grape 'Solaris'
items.growersTips:
Plant Solaris in your sunniest, south-facing spot to help this early-ripening grape beat UK autumns.
Prune hard in January while dormant to prevent the vine bleeding sap and losing its strength.
Pinch out the vigorous leafy shoots in July so the vine channels its energy into ripening grapes.
Watch out for powdery mildew in damp UK summers, keeping the center of the vine open for airflow.
Grow Solaris in poor, well-drained soil because too much richness just leads to leaves, not fruit.
items.description: Very early disease-resistant white grape.

items.name: Grape 'Triomphe'
items.growersTips:
To get the best crop in the UK climate, grow this vine against a sunny, south or west-facing wall.
Prune in midwinter when fully dormant to prevent bleeding, training it to a single or double guyot.
Water deeply at the base weekly during summer dry spells, but stop once the grapes start to colour.
Pinch out the tips of leafy shoots two leaves past each flower cluster in summer to boost fruiting.
Watch out for powdery mildew in damp UK weather, so space out the branches to keep air flowing well.

items.name: Grape 'Vroege van der Laan'

Plant this early white grape against a south-facing wall to trap the essential British summer heat.
Prune in midwinter while dormant to stop the vine bleeding sap, leaving just two strong main rods.
Thin out the dense summer canopy in July so the precious UK sun can actually reach the grape bunches.
Water deeply at the base during dry spells but keep the foliage dry to prevent powdery mildew issues.
Throw a fine net over the vine in late August to stop wasps and blackbirds stealing your sweet crop.
items.description: Dutch outdoor white grape.

items.name: Grape 'Cascade'
items.growersTips:
Prune your Cascade in January to avoid bleeding sap, keeping only one or two strong fruiting rods.
Plant your vine against a south-facing wall to help this early-ripening grape cope with UK damp.
Mulch with well-rotted manure in March to feed the roots, keeping it clear of the main stem.
Watch out for powdery mildew in muggy British summers and space out the leaves to improve airflow.
Drape netting over the ripening black bunches in August before local wasps and blackbirds ruin them.
items.description: Hardy outdoor red grape.

items.name: Grape 'Lakemont'

Plant this seedless white grape against a sunny south-facing wall to help the fruit ripen in the UK.
Prune your vine in mid-winter while dormant to prevent the sap bleeding and ruining spring growth.
Cut back the leafy shoots to two leaves past each grape bunch in July to let the summer sun in.
Mulch with well-rotted manure in spring but keep it away from the stem to avoid collar rot.
Watch out for powdery mildew in damp UK summers by watering only at the base, never the leaves.
items.description: Seedless outdoor white grape.

items.name: Grape 'New York Muscat'
items.growersTips:
Plant this grape against a south-facing brick wall to trap the warmth needed for UK fruit ripening.
Prune your vine strictly in midwinter to prevent the sap bleeding that weakens plants in spring.
Pinch out the growing tips two leaves past each flower cluster to focus energy into sweet grapes.
Water deeply at the base weekly during dry spells, but keep the foliage dry to prevent downy mildew.
Thin out the dense summer canopy to ensure maximum sunlight and air reach the ripening bunches.
items.description: Muscat-flavoured outdoor grape.

items.name: Grape 'Suffolk Red'
items.growersTips:
Plant your Suffolk Red against a sunny south-facing wall to trap the heat it needs to ripen in the UK.
Prune in midwinter when fully dormant to prevent the vine from bleeding sap and losing its strength.
Thin out the dense summer foliage in July so the precious UK sunshine can actually reach the grapes.
Water deeply at the base during dry summer spells, but stop once the red berries start to colour up.

items.description: Seedless outdoor red grape.

items.name: Fig
items.growersTips:
Restrict root growth by planting in a buried 40cm pot to force energy into fruit rather than leaves.
Prune in late winter to shape, then pinch out new shoot tips at five leaves in June to boost yield.
Protect tiny pea-sized young overwintering figs with fleece from November to March against UK frost.
Water container-grown figs deeply and consistently during summer fruit-swell to prevent fruit drop.
Plant against a south or west-facing brick wall to maximize heat absorption in the cool UK climate.
items.description: Reference parent species for the Fig cultivars.

items.name: Fig 'Brown Turkey'
items.growersTips:
To stop it growing wild and encourage fruit, plant it in a buried container to restrict its roots.
Prune your fig in late winter, always leaving the tiny pea-sized baby figs at the tips of branches.
Protect those tiny overwintering baby figs from harsh UK frosts by wrapping the branches in fleece.
Give it a weekly deep soak in dry summer spells, but stop watering once the figs start to ripen.
Plant it against a south or west-facing brick wall to soak up the maximum amount of British sun.
items.description: Reliable hardy UK fig, brown skin.

items.name: Fig 'Brunswick'
items.growersTips:
Plant your Brunswick in a soil-restricting pit or pot to stop leafy growth and force heavy fruiting.
Tie your Brunswick flat against a south-facing wall to trap the UK sun and ripen those massive figs.
Prune your fig in late winter, leaving the tiny pea-sized embryo figs at the tips for next summer.
Protect the tiny overwintering figlets from harsh UK frosts by wrapping the branches in fleece.
Water your Brunswick deeply when the fruit starts to swell, but keep it dry early in the season.

Plant your fig in a bottomless pot sunk into the ground to restrict roots and boost fruit yield.
Grow this variety against a sunny, south-facing brick wall to help the early summer breba crop ripen.
Prune in late winter by removing one-third of older branches to encourage new, fruit-bearing wood.
Protect the tiny, pea-sized embryo figs over winter using fleece to ensure a good harvest next year.

Prune in late winter when dormant, removing older wood to let sunlight ripen the new green figs.

Wrap the branches in fleece during frosty winters to protect the delicate young spring figs.

Prune in late winter to shape it, then pinch out new shoots in June to encourage baby figs.
Wrap the branches in fleece during freezing winter snaps to protect the tiny overwintering crop.
